dietEvidence.body: The skull is unknown, so direct dietary evidence is unavailable. Herbivory is inferred from the animal's relationships and the preserved postcranial anatomy.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A nodosaurid known from a partial skeleton with bony armour. The original material is fragmentary and the animal’s proportions are reconstructed.
summary: A nodosaurid known from a partial skeleton with bony armour. The original material is fragmentary and the animal’s proportions are reconstructed.

discovery.body: Named by Marsh, 1889. The type and only well-established specimen is YPM 1815, a partial postcranial skeleton from the Frontier Formation (Belle Fourche Member) at Como Bluff, Wyoming. The skull is unknown.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: YPM 1815 includes dorsal and caudal vertebrae, ribs, part of the pelvis, fragmentary forelimbs, a partial hindlimb and osteoderms. The skull is not known, so cranial anatomy and diet cannot be directly observed.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Frontier Formation (Belle Fourche Member), Como Bluff, Wyoming records the species in the Late Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈100–97 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on the specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The body armour consists of keeled plates and low spines, including a sacral shield. The osteoderms are preserved, but their complete arrangement and the animal's live profile are reconstructed.

anatomy.title: Body plan
anatomy.body: The species is reconstructed as quadrupedal from the preserved limb bones and comparison with other nodosaurids; the posture is not observed.

behaviour.body: No direct behavioural evidence. Quadrupedality is inferred from limb anatomy. Armour function is inferred, not observed.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a partial postcranial skeleton with armour; the skull is not well represented. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The species is known from one partial postcranial skeleton, YPM 1815, from the Frontier Formation (Belle Fourche Member) at Como Bluff, Wyoming; the skull is unknown. The formation was corrected from the Mowry Shale. Size, armour arrangement and body proportions are reconstructed from a fragmentary specimen and comparisons with relatives.
